title: Bug: Boolean values bypass integer validation in `isinstance(..., int)` checks
body:
In Python, `bool` is a subclass of `int`. Because of this, using `isinstance(val, int)` without also checking `not isinstance(val, bool)` will incorrectly accept boolean values as valid integers. This issue is present in several places:

1. `pyxle/config.py`: `cors.maxAge` validation uses `if not isinstance(max_age, int) or max_age < 0:`.
2. `pyxle/devserver/registry.py`: `loader_line` uses `if not isinstance(loader_line, int):`.
3. `pyxle/devserver/registry.py`: `websocket_line` uses `if not isinstance(websocket_line, int):`.
4. `pyxle/compiler/jsx_parser.py`: `error_line` uses `error_line=error_line if isinstance(error_line, int) else None`.
5. `pyxle/devserver/csrf.py`: `port if isinstance(port, int) else None`

**Recommendation:** 
Update these checks to explicitly exclude boolean values, e.g., `if not isinstance(val, int) or isinstance(val, bool):`, similar to how other parts of the codebase correctly handle this (e.g., `requests`, `window`, etc.).
